questions.q: Why does this capstone use scheduled batch COPY INTO loads instead of Snowpipe?
options: Snowpipe cannot load CSV files
Driftwood's actual requirement is a once-daily refresh, not sub-minute freshness -- Snowpipe's continuous-loading infrastructure would solve a problem the business doesn't have
Snowpipe requires a different Snowflake edition that Driftwood doesn't have
COPY INTO is always faster than Snowpipe regardless of use case
questions.explain: The decision follows directly from the stated business requirement (daily, not real-time) -- the same right-sized-tool reasoning the AWS Capstone applies when choosing a nightly export over continuous CDC.

questions.q: What does ON_ERROR = 'ABORT_STATEMENT' actually do during a COPY INTO load?
options: Automatically fixes malformed rows before loading
Pauses the load and waits for manual approval
Skips bad rows silently and loads everything else without any record of what failed
Rejects the entire load if even one row fails to parse, rather than silently loading a partial result
questions.explain: ABORT_STATEMENT means the whole load fails loudly rather than quietly loading a partial, inconsistent day's data -- a deliberate choice for a financial/subscriber dataset.

questions.q: What does running a COPY INTO with VALIDATION_MODE = 'RETURN_ERRORS' actually do?
options: Reports which rows would fail and why, without actually loading any data
Permanently deletes rows that fail validation
Runs the load twice to confirm consistency
Loads all valid rows and silently discards invalid ones
questions.explain: VALIDATION_MODE is a dry-run check -- it surfaces exactly what would fail before any real load happens, which the Airflow DAG uses as a pre-check.

questions.q: What naming discipline does the date-partitioned stage path (e.g. dt=2026-10-17) follow from this catalog's other capstones?
options: Date-partitioning the raw landing path, the same pattern used in other capstones like AWS Capstone
Storing all files in one flat directory with no partitioning
A random unique identifier per file, with no date information
Partitioning by file size instead of date
questions.explain: Date-partitioned paths are a consistent, reused pattern across this catalog's capstones for predictable, prunable raw-zone organization.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's the real cost of defaulting to a more sophisticated ingestion tool than the business actually needs?
options: There is no real cost -- more sophisticated tools are always strictly better
Unnecessary operational complexity to stand up and maintain infrastructure for a freshness requirement nobody asked for
It would reduce Snowflake's storage costs
It would make the data load faster for no reason
questions.explain: Matching the tool to the actual requirement avoids unnecessary operational overhead -- the same discipline applied throughout this catalog's capstone courses.
